sections.text: भूतग्रामः स एवायं भूत्वा भूत्वा प्रलीयते।
The same multitude of beings, which have lived on earth so often, all are dissolved as the night of the universe approaches, to issue forth anew when morning breaks. Thus is it ordained.
In truth, therefore, there is the Eternal Unmanifest, which is beyond and above the Unmanifest Spirit of Creation, which is never destroyed when all these beings perish.
The wise say that the Unmanifest and Indestructible is the highest goal of all; when once That is reached, there is no return. That is My Blessed Home.

We had been discussing chapter 8, Akshara Brahma Yoga Yoga of Imperishable Brahman as we have seen that we are trying to understand the nature of the supreme reality, so we have to do some heavy lifting here to understand the underlying concepts. In the beginning, we heard from Bhagavan that Brahman is imperishable, immutable, and self-knowledge is its nature. What is the nature of Brahman? It is self-knowledge. It does not require any other aid to understand it. It is self-effulgent.
Its very nature is self knowledge. With its creative force, it works to create things and beings. What his work is that which creates these things and beings. That Brahman which is imperishable, its nature is self knowledge. With its own creative force, it works to create things and beings. Then what is nature of the things and beings that Brahman has created?
Brahman is imperishable, but anything that is created by its creative force is perishable. That because the very act of creation gives it a birth date, its now created. Something is created, therefore it will have its own life. Then it will get destroyed. It will have a limited shelf life as we call it, no matter how long. That is what makes those things and beings function as they are.
The Daivam is that same Brahman remaining within each created entity -- that Daivam makes the thing or being possible as a creation. And when these things and beings are reacting with each other, its only possible because Brahman remains present as the Yajnam in all the activities -- that Supreme Being is present in every action. Therefore all activities are possible in this world of created beings. The analogy we have heard before is like my dream. I as the conscious being have experiences in my waking world.
The same experiences at night gets all jumbled up. My mind creates its own world. Out of my own mind, I create my own world. That mind by itself creates various entities, things and beings in My dream. Those entities are acting in the dream because I am in and through available to project the dream. But when I wake up, all those entities, things and beings are now unmanifest.
Till next time I go to sleep again and dream again. So this is what we have seen is how the overall cosmos is functioning at the level of Brahman. Him remaining supreme, unchangeable with his self knowledge, with his own creative force, he works to create these things and beings. These things and beings, their Gunana Dharma. I studied chemistry in Gujarati -- because I studied all throughout my school days and college days in Gujarati medium. In chemistry they used to ask us, Padarthana Gunadharmanu Varnan karo -- describe the characteristics and nature of this substance. So there are two things every substance has: Guna and Dharma.
Guna is the basic characteristics of that substance or a thing or a being. And Dharma is the nature of that substance depending on guna. So what is my Dharma is depending on my gunas. The gunas which I have as an entity creates my Dharma. So Guna and Dharma are related to each other. So Brahman creating things and beings.
Each thing and being has its own Dharma, Guna and Dharma. This Guna and Dharma continues to change as we acquire more impressions. So my guna before I went to architecture school has nothing to do with architecture. In fact, I was not even aware of what architecture is all about. So at that point my Dharma had nothing to do with architectural knowledge or practice. More I acquired the architectural knowledge.
My gunas changed, so my Dharma changed. So now I practice architecture. So Guna Dharma is constantly changing this evolutionary path a thing or being takes in the creation itself. So Bhagavan said that this creation is now guided by its own laws, where each thing and being is driven by their own Guna and Dharma. What will be my next state of existence? It depends on the gunas which I am creating through my experiences -- as a practicing architect or as a Bhagavad Gita student.
So my next state of existence can only be evolution from a present state. It cannot completely change overnight from where I am today. So thats the evolutionary path each thing and being in the creation takes. So from some stardust, my original evolution started and then that keeps changing. Gunanayana Dharma came to this level where I am today. I read in some one of these popular science books that our atoms in the body continues to change.
They are not the same atoms, because our bodys cells change every few years. And they said it is possible that the atoms which existed in Shakespeares body or Ramas body or Krishnas body have passed through my body at one point -- because there is a finite amount of energy, a finite amount of matter, and all things and beings are created out of that. The nature of this cosmos is that one thing changes into the shape and form of another and continues.
So where I am today is the product of my past -- from that stardust to who I am today. My future would be the product of my present plus my past. The advice then given to us is this: if you want to accelerate this evolution and not go through this gradual path of changing Guna and Dharma, you can directly relate to the Source. We have seen that Brahman is imperishable, immutable, and created this universe out of his own creative force as the efficient cause.
Material cause was the only thing available to Brahman, which is his own self. He created this universe out of his own self. And each creation has limited life. Creation remains perishable, but the underlying material which creates this universe remains imperishable. So either I can identify with my Guna and a Dharma today and then take a step next forward in the same path of my evolution, or I can short circuit this whole cycle and go straight to my source where I started. So thats the advice in this chapter.
At the time of death -- death is the end of this state of existence. The death of today will create tomorrow. At the time of this transition, whatever I think would be my next state of existence, thats what I will become. Bhagawan said, you can focus directly on the Source and become the Source. Up to Brahma Loka, the world of Brahma, everything has coming and going. As long as we are within the realm of this Prakriti -- which is made up of nothing but the total things and beings in this world -- I will keep recycling from one state of existence to another.
And we have said how long this will continue -- as long as Brahma is creating and dissolving. We see our own day and night in our day-to-day activities. Day is the active part of my life. Night is the inactive part of my life. Superimposing the same concept on Brahmaji, the total creator:
I am the creator of my world. You are the creator of your world. She is the creator of her world. When you put all things and beings together, all the ideas and vasanas and thoughts together create cosmic mind. The cosmic mind has the latency to create this cosmos. And thats called Hiranyagarpa, the golden embryo, which is all the possibilities of creating everything that is in this cosmos that continues to be go in the cycles of activity and inactivity.
When Brahma is actively creating, its his day. When he takes rest and is inactive, its night for him. We superimpose our experience: my day is activity, my night is inactivity. Its not so different now with nightlife, but 5,000 years ago they probably didnt have nightlife. So what is Brahmas day? Brahmas day is a thousand eons. So for thousand eons this activity of creation continues. Things changing from one thing to another to another. And then Brahmaji takes rest. All the things which he has created now goes into dormant state. Not destroyed, but in a dormant state.
Just as I, the architect, goes into dormant state from Friday to Sunday. But that doesnt mean the architect in me has died. Architect in me will wake up on Monday morning and start all over again. So all the ideas and thoughts and vasanas in this total mind go into hibernation, into a dormant state. How long does that last? Another thousand eons.
So we did some calculation the other day: 4.32 billion years is one day. A thousand of these makes 4.32 billion years, and you take two of them -- day and night -- thats 8.6-something billion years, one complete cycle. So when you think about your journey, this is what continues from day to night, day and night, from one state of existence to another. And if you as the entity are not really happy about it, then there is an escape hatch: take refuge in me, identify with the Source.
As long as Im watching David Copperfield performing magic, its wonderful to watch and get enchanted by it and then keep thinking, how does he do it? Till one day I show up when he is preparing for his show and say, I want to be your apprentice, sir. And he takes me and then he shows me and then I see how all these tricks are done and then all magic is gone. Now Im not confused. Now when hes cutting the lady in half, I know exactly what hes doing. Till that time, I have to keep coming back. Till I reach Brahma Loka, the Creators own world, I will be coming back into the same cycle. But then when I reach there and identify with the source, I will become one with that. So it gives us a scale. My quest in life to achieve happiness is not a short-term thing, even though I put it in short-term goals and long-term goals. But in the end I want happiness. If you just extend that quest to Brahmas day and night and work towards your goal, the only way to achieve that is to identify with the source. Avyakta d vyaktayaha Sarvaha prabhavanti aha Agame. So all those things in beings with all their guna and Dharma are in dormant state. When Brahmaj is inactive, which we consider as a dissolution. Pralaya, Vishnu, lying in a Kshira, Shira, Samudra, milky ocean.
There are no vasanas, pure Sattva, then there is no activity. If it is pure Sattva, there is no activity. Rajas and Tamas has to be there. So when you are in a pure state of Sattva, there is no activity. But all other things in being there in dormant state. All the other thoughts are in dormant state.
Just as when I go to sleep, all my thoughts about what Im going to be doing next week are in dormant state. Not that Ive forgotten anything about it. Im just in dormant state. As soon as I wake up on Monday morning, we all come into being and becomes my work and my activity and my creation. Avyakta, vyaktaha, sarvaha prabhavanti ahaha made the arrival of the day. All those who were unmanifest now becomes manifest in all those who are manifest during the day.

These verses introduce the concept of Guna and Dharma, the characteristics that define who we are and the duties that arise from them. The teaching that where I am today is the product of my past and my future would be the product of my present offers both responsibility and hope. You are not trapped by your current limitations; you are simply at one point on an evolutionary journey that stretches across lifetimes. The fascinating scientific observation that our atoms are constantly recycling, that atoms once in Shakespeares or Krishnas body may have passed through yours, points to the material interconnectedness of all existence. This week, reflect on your own Guna-Dharma evolution: What qualities did you have ten years ago that have now transformed? What new capacities have emerged? What qualities are you currently cultivating that will shape your future self?
Verse 20 reveals there is something beyond even the unmanifest Prakriti from which creation emerges: Paras tasmat tu bhavo anyo avyakto avyaktat sanatanah, Beyond this unmanifest is another Unmanifest, eternal, which does not perish when all beings perish. This is the ultimate goal, not just a better position within the cycle, but transcendence of the cycle itself. The analogy of watching a magician perform is apt: as long as you sit in the audience, you are enchanted by the illusion. But when you become the magicians apprentice and learn how the tricks work, the magic dissolves into understanding. Verse 21 promises: Yam prapya na nivartante, having reached this, one does not return. This is not a distant goal. The teaching offers a short circuit: rather than evolving slowly through countless incarnations, you can go directly to the Source through knowledge and devotion. Today, ask yourself: Am I content to improve my position within the dream, or am I ready to wake up?
